title: Web Nostr DNS control-plane client and run tracker
observed_behavior: The web DNS store had read-only REST collection loaders for DNS zones, endpoints, drift, and policies.
Web Nostr helpers already supported signed publishRequest, status subscriptions, and explicit result-event awaiting.
Browser code did not expose DNS command constants or a DNS run tracker for kinds 5941-5944, 6941, and 7941-7944.
intended_behavior: Browser callers can publish DNS zone create, policy apply, record override, and drift remediate commands as signed Nostr request events.
DNS command runs expose publish OK outcomes, accepted/rejected relay lists, request event id, status events, terminal result payloads, and CLOSED/AUTH errors.
Terminal completion is driven only by explicit DNS result events; no REST write path or timeout-as-completion behavior is introduced.
